title: Clifford bound for subcanonical clusters with a splitting correction
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $X$ be a nonempty connected projective reduced $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-kun-projective, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-pure-dimension]. Assume $X$ is smooth except at ordinary nodes, meaning that at every singular closed point its completed local $k$-algebra is $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Write $h^i(X,F)=\dim_kH^i(X,F)$ for Zariski module cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. Assume that for every decomposition $X=A\cup B$ into nonempty reduced unions of components with no common component, $\dim_k\Gamma(A\times_XB,\mathcal O_{A\times_XB})\ge2$ [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-pc-fibre-product]. Put $p_a(X)=1-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-euler-characteristic]. For every subcanonical zero-dimensional closed subscheme $T\subseteq X$, with ideal $I_T$, dualizing line $\omega_X$ and splitting index $r(T)$ as defined in [def-sfb-subcanonical-splitting-index], put $\ell(T)=\dim_k\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. Then
$$h^0(X,I_T\otimes\omega_X)\le p_a(X)-\tfrac12\ell(T)+\tfrac12r(T).$$
The subscheme $T$ need not be Cartier or reduced.

source.place: Theorem 3.7, inequality (9), printed pp.242--246, specialized to reduced nodal curves; numerical two-connectedness is boundary-node length; local PDF WANTED, author-hosted primary text read online.

proof.text: Put $p=p_a(X)$, $R=r(T)$, $v(U)=h^0(X,I_U\otimes\omega_X)$ and $c(U)=2p-\ell(U)-2v(U)$. We must prove $c(T)\ge-R$. By the residual-duality lemma, all these numbers are finite, $v(U)\le h^0(X,\omega_X)=p$, and $0\le\ell(U)\le2p-2$ for every subcanonical $U$. Thus only finitely many integer pairs $(c(U),\ell(U))$ occur. If $c(T)\ge0$, the assertion follows from $R\ge0$. Otherwise set $\Sigma_R=\{U:U\text{ subcanonical},\ r(U)\le R\}$ and choose, among all subcanonical $U$ with $r(U)\le R$, a cluster $S$ minimizing $c(U)$ and, among minimizers, maximizing $\ell(U)$. This is selection from a finite nonempty set of integer pairs, not a compactness assertion about a parameter scheme. We have $c(S)\le c(T)<0$. No residual-invariance closure is assumed for $\Sigma_R$; the later union will be proved to lie in this same class before invoking extremality.

source.place: Theorem 3.7 proof, beginning and Step 2, pp.243 and 246; bounded integer-pair selection made explicit.

proof.text: The empty cluster has $v=p$ and $c=0$. If $\ell(U)=2p-2$, residual duality gives $U^*=\varnothing$, $v(U)=1$ and $c(U)=0$. Hence $0<\ell(S)<2p-2$. For each component partition $\mathcal P$ with $|\mathcal P|-1>R$, put $W_{\mathcal P}=\sum_{A\in\mathcal P}(V_S)_A\subset V_S$, using the supported subspaces of the splitting definition. Disjoint generic supports make this sum direct: a sum zero vanishes on each component, and a section of a line on the reduced curve vanishing at all generic points is zero. If $W_{\mathcal P}=V_S$, the partition would be admissible, contrary to $r(S)\le R$. Thus these finitely many $W_{\mathcal P}$ are proper linear subspaces. Choose $s$ outside all of them, nonzero at every component generic point, and in the moving-component lemma's nonempty open. Such a choice exists: the generic-point zero loci are also proper linear subspaces, and in coordinates each of these finitely many nonempty opens contains a principal open defined by a nonzero polynomial. Their product is nonzero and has a nonzero value over the infinite field $k$, by induction on the number of variables and the one-variable root bound.

source.place: Theorem 3.7 (9), proof Step 1; agent correction of the use of Remark 2.18 and Lemma 3.1.

proof.text: Let $S^*$ be the residual of this $s$ and let $U=S\cup S^*$, so $V_U=V_S\cap V_{S^*}$ inside the canonical section space. Evaluating the inclusion $F_S\hookrightarrow\omega_X$ at $s$ gives $s\in V_{S^*}$ in the residual construction; hence $s\in V_U$ is generically nonzero and $U$ is subcanonical. If a partition $\mathcal P$ with $|\mathcal P|-1>R$ were admissible for $V_U$, decomposing $s$ in its supported summands would put $s\in W_{\mathcal P}$, since $V_U\subseteq V_S$. This contradicts its choice. Since $U\supseteq S\ne\varnothing$, its splitting index uses the largest-admissible-partition formula, and $r(U)\le R$. All hypotheses of the corrected nesting lemma now hold: $c(S)<0$, minimal Clifford index and maximal length in $\Sigma_R$, and the verified union bound. It follows that $S^*\subseteq S$. This argument does not compare $r(S^*)$ with $r(S)$ and does not use monotonicity of $r$.

source.place: Theorem 3.7 (9), proof Step 1; agent correction of the use of Remark 2.18 and Lemma 3.1.

proof.text: The ideal inclusion $I_S\subseteq I_{S^*}$ from $S^*\subseteq S$ gives $V_S\subseteq V_{S^*}$ as subspaces of canonical sections. It gives the same inclusion of their images on every component. If the image of $V_S$ on some $\Gamma$ had dimension at least two, both images would have dimension at least two. The moving-component lemma would give $\ell(S^*)=2$ and $v(S^*)=p-1$, so $c(S^*)=2p-2-2(p-1)=0$. Residual duality says $c(S^*)=c(S)<0$, a contradiction. Every component image of $V_S$ is therefore at most one-dimensional; subcanonicity supplies a section nonzero at its generic point, so each image has dimension exactly one.

source.place: Theorem 3.7 proof Step 1, Cases 1 and 2, p.243; nested residual forces the rank-one branch.

proof.text:
Write $q=r(S)\le R$ and $d=2p-2-\ell(S)\ge0$. Apply the rank-one component lemma with the actual restriction images just verified. It gives $v(S)=q+1$. If $q=0$, then $c(S)=2p-\ell(S)-2=d\ge0$, contradicting $c(S)<0$. If $q>0$, its degree bound gives $d\ge q$, and consequently
$$c(S)=2p-\ell(S)-2(q+1)=d-2q\ge-q\ge-R.$$
Since $c(T)\ge c(S)$, we obtain $c(T)\ge-R$ also in the negative case. Rearranging $2p-\ell(T)-2v(T)\ge-R$ proves the stated inequality. Every residual and restriction argument allowed non-Cartier and nonreduced clusters.
